title: Atractylenolide III alleviates cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury by targeting Keap1 to activate the Nrf2/HO-1 pathway.
authors: Guo, Roujia; Quan, Siqi; Yan, Xiangli; Jia, Yapeng; Wang, Nuo; Bu, Jingjing; Zhao, Yufang; Su, Linzhe; Yue, Zhouli; Wang, Jiahui; Li, Zibo; Li, Yucheng
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究药物ATL III靶向Keap1激活Nrf2/HO-1通路减轻脑缺血再灌注损伤，虽涉及蛋白-蛋白互作（Keap1-Nrf2）及分子对接/MD模拟，但核心对象非蛋白质-DNA互作，与TF-DNA课题关联较弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Atractylenolide III (ATL III), a natural sesquiterpene lactone, exhibits neuroprotective properties against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI), but its underlying mechanism remains unclear. PURPOSE: To identify the pharmacological target and elucidate the mechanism of ATL III in CIRI protection. METHODS: Middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) in mice and oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R) in HT22 cells were employed to evaluate the protective effects of ATL III on neurological function, oxidative stress, and apoptosis. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, surface plasmon resonance, and molecular dynamics were used to identify its direct target. Molecular mechanisms were validated using Western blot, immunofluorescence, and a pharmacological inhibitor both in vitro and in vivo. RESULTS: ATL III (10, 20, 40 mg/kg) significantly reduced infarct volume in MCAO/R mice from 42 % to 33 %, 27 %, and 20 %, and decreased neurological scores from 13 to 9, 7, and 5. Histology revealed alleviated hippocampal neuronal damage. In HT22 cells, ATL III decreased OGD/R-induced apoptosis, lowered ROS levels from 374 % to 202 %, increased SOD and GSH, and reduced MDA levels. Keap1 was identified as a direct target; ATL III disrupted the Keap1-Nrf2 interaction, reduced Keap1 protein levels, increased Nrf2 expression and nuclear translocation, and upregulated HO-1 expression. Nrf2 inhibition with ML385 abolished these antioxidative and neuroprotective effects in both models. CONCLUSION: ATL III protects against CIRI by directly targeting Keap1 and activating the Nrf2/HO-1 pathway. Given its favorable safety profile and blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability, ATL III holds promising translational potential as a plant-derived prophylactic agent for ischemic stroke.
abstract_zh: 背景：白术内酯III（ATL III）是一种天然倍半萜内酯，对脑缺血再灌注损伤（CIRI）具有神经保护作用，但其潜在机制尚不清楚。目的：确定ATL III在CIRI保护中的药理学靶点并阐明其机制。方法：采用小鼠大脑中动脉闭塞/再灌注（MCAO/R）模型和HT22细胞氧糖剥夺/再灌注（OGD/R）模型，评估ATL III对神经功能、氧化应激和凋亡的保护作用。通过网络药理学、分子对接、表面等离子体共振和分子动力学（molecular dynamics）确定其直接靶点。通过Western blot、免疫荧光及药理学抑制剂在体外和体内验证分子机制。结果：ATL III（10、20、40 mg/kg）显著将MCAO/R小鼠的梗死体积从42%分别降至33%、27%和20%，并将神经功能评分从13降至9、7和5。组织学显示海马神经元损伤得到缓解。在HT22细胞中，ATL III降低了OGD/R诱导的凋亡，将ROS水平从374%降至202%，增加了SOD和GSH，并降低了MDA水平。Keap1被确定为直接靶点；ATL III破坏了Keap1-Nrf2相互作用，降低了Keap1蛋白水平，增加了Nrf2表达和核转位，并上调了HO-1表达。在两种模型中，Nrf2抑制剂ML385均消除了这些抗氧化和神经保护效应。结论：ATL III通过直接靶向Keap1并激活Nrf2/HO-1通路来保护CIRI。鉴于其良好的安全性和血脑屏障（BBB）通透性，ATL III作为植物来源的缺血性卒中预防性药物具有广阔的转化潜力。
